parsed.observation: GET /api/v2/orders/123 returned 200 with another user's order body; my session is for user_id=1, the response body shows user_id=2

hypotheses.given: Authenticated session for user_id=1; order 123 is known to belong to user_id=2
hypotheses.if: I send GET /api/v2/orders/123 with my session cookie
hypotheses.then: The response body contains the order data with user_id=2 shown explicitly
hypotheses.because: The endpoint checks authentication (session is valid) but not authorization (does not verify the requesting user owns the order); it serves the requested object regardless of ownership
hypotheses.refute_on: Server returns 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found when accessing another user's order; or response contains only the requesting user's orders
hypotheses.cheap_test: curl -s -H 'Cookie: session=USER1_SESSION' 'https://target/api/v2/orders/124' | grep -q 'user_id.*[^1]' && echo VULNERABLE || echo SAFE

hypotheses.given: A reverse proxy or CDN caches responses; order 123 was previously requested by user_id=2
hypotheses.if: I request the same order ID while a cached response from another user exists
hypotheses.then: I receive the cached response containing user_id=2 data despite my session being user_id=1
hypotheses.because: The cache key is derived only from the URL path/query, not from user context (session, User-ID header); the proxy serves the same cached object to all users
hypotheses.refute_on: Response includes Vary header covering auth context; or Cache-Control: private/no-cache is present; or requesting with Cache-Control: no-cache returns the correct user's order
hypotheses.cheap_test: curl -s -H 'Cookie: session=USER1_SESSION' -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' 'https://target/api/v2/orders/123' | grep -q 'user_id.*[^1]' && echo CACHE_ISSUE || echo SAFE

hypotheses.given: The endpoint accepts additional query parameters or request body fields
hypotheses.if: I send GET /api/v2/orders/123?user_id=2 or include a user_id field in the request
hypotheses.then: The parameter overrides the authorization logic and the endpoint returns user_id=2 data
hypotheses.because: Mass assignment or insufficient parameter filtering allows injecting sensitive fields; the authorization layer uses the injected parameter instead of the session user
hypotheses.refute_on: Extra parameters are silently ignored; authorization still validates against session user_id; response shows only the requesting user's data
hypotheses.cheap_test: curl -s -H 'Cookie: session=USER1_SESSION' 'https://target/api/v2/orders/123?user_id=2' | grep -q 'user_id.*2' && echo VULNERABLE || echo SAFE

hypotheses.given: The authorization check and data fetch are separate operations without atomic locking
hypotheses.if: I send two concurrent requests for the same order from the same session
hypotheses.then: One or both requests bypass the ownership check due to a race condition between validation and retrieval
hypotheses.because: A TOCTOU (Time-of-check-time-of-use) window exists; between the moment authorization is checked and the moment data is fetched, the request or session context can be manipulated or the check can be skipped
hypotheses.refute_on: All concurrent requests consistently succeed with correct authorization or consistently fail; adding timing delays does not change the outcome; data is always correct for the requester
hypotheses.cheap_test: seq 10 | xargs -P 5 -I{} curl -s -H 'Cookie: session=USER1_SESSION' 'https://target/api/v2/orders/123' | grep -c 'user_id.*2' | grep -q '[1-9]' && echo VULNERABLE || echo SAFE

hypotheses.given: The application accepts multiple authentication/authorization signals (session + header)
hypotheses.if: I send GET /api/v2/orders/123 with my session (user_id=1) AND a custom header like X-User-ID: 2
hypotheses.then: The response contains user_id=2 data, indicating the header was used for authorization instead of the session
hypotheses.because: The endpoint has overlapping authentication mechanisms with conflicting precedence; the custom header is trusted more than the session or is not validated against it
hypotheses.refute_on: The custom header is ignored; authorization always uses the session user; response contains only the requesting user's data; server returns 400 or rejects the custom header
hypotheses.cheap_test: curl -s -H 'Cookie: session=USER1_SESSION' -H 'X-User-ID: 2' 'https://target/api/v2/orders/123' | grep -q 'user_id.*2' && echo VULNERABLE || echo SAFE

parsed.notes: All five hypotheses explain the core observation (accessing user_id=2 data while authenticated as user_id=1). They span different bug classes (IDOR, cache-poisoning, mass-assignment, race, auth-bypass) to avoid tunnel vision and satisfy the forcing function in § 2 of hypothesis-driven.md. The cheap tests use minimal curl invocations with grep patterns to detect user_id=2 in responses. Each refute_on clause specifies the observation that would disprove the hypothesis and guide the next iteration of the model."
